IP/User-Agent Info

Check IP, user-agent, language, and timezone quickly.

A browser cannot resolve its own public IP, so this page calls api.ipify.org, which exposes your IP to that service. User-Agent, language, timezone and platform are read locally.

IP and User-Agent inspection

Review current browser IP, User-Agent, language, and timezone values to reproduce environment-specific issues.

Collect support details

Gather the browser string, language, and timezone that support or QA teams need for reproduction.

Check network path

Confirm the externally visible IP when using a VPN, proxy, office network, or mobile network.

Copy-ready environment data

Use the values in logs, support tickets, and QA notes after reviewing what should be shared.

Errors you will hit

The IP does not match your location

A VPN, corporate proxy, or mobile carrier NAT shows the exit server address. IP-based geolocation is indicative only.

The OS version is frozen at 10_15_7

Chrome reduces the detail it reports in the User-Agent for privacy. Newer macOS versions still report 10_15_7, so use Client Hints when you need the real version.

Things to check

IP is not exact location

IP-based location can differ from physical location because of VPNs, proxies, carriers, and office networks.

User-Agent is reduced

Modern browsers may reduce or freeze User-Agent details for privacy. Feature detection is more reliable for capability checks.

Public and private IPs differ

The value shown is your public IP as seen from the internet. A browser cannot read the 192.168 address behind your router. For a firewall allowlist this is the right value; for finding a device on the LAN it is not.

User-Agent is no longer reliable

Browsers are freezing and reducing the UA string to limit fingerprinting. Code that parses UA for version or platform will increasingly be wrong. Use feature detection instead.

VPNs and proxies show a different value

Behind a corporate VPN or proxy, the IP shown is that exit server's address. This is how people end up allowlisting the office IP when they meant their home one. Disconnect and check again.

More: step-by-step usage and worked examples

How to use it

  1. Open the page and inspect the current browser environment values.
  2. Refresh after changing VPN or network settings to compare the visible IP.
  3. Record User-Agent, browser language, and timezone when asking someone to reproduce a bug.
  4. Before sharing, decide whether exposing IP or internal network details is appropriate.
